# queuedesk

The ticket queue of a small help desk (Java 17, standard library only). Priorities run from 1 (most urgent) to 4, time is a
plain tick counter that the desk advances by hand. The tests are a plain `TestMain` (no JUnit):
`javac -d build $(find . -name '*.java') && java -cp build TestMain`.

## Layout

* `src/queuedesk/Desk.java`: the queue.
* `src/queuedesk/Ticket.java`: one ticket.
* `test/TestMain.java`: tests.

## Basics

* `Desk.open(subject, priority)` creates and returns a `Ticket` with ids 1, 2, 3, ... The subject must not be blank (it is
  stripped) and the priority must be 1 to 4 (`IllegalArgumentException`). A new ticket is open and remembers the tick it was
  opened at.
* `Ticket` has `id()`, `subject()`, `priority()`, `openedAt()` and `closed()`. `Desk.get(id)` returns a ticket
  (`NoSuchElementException` for an unknown id).
* `Desk.tick()` advances the clock by one, `Desk.now()` returns it (it starts at 0).
* `Desk.openTickets()` lists the open tickets, most urgent first and by id within one priority. `Desk.next()` returns the first
  of them as an `Optional<Ticket>`.
* `Desk.close(id)` closes an open ticket and returns it (an already closed ticket is an `IllegalStateException`). `Desk.count(open)`
  counts the open (`true`) or closed (`false`) tickets.

## Assigning tickets to agents

`assign(id, agent)` (unknown ticket, blank agent, closed ticket, in that order), `Ticket.agent()`, `workload(agent)` and `next(agent)` (unassigned tickets or the agent's own).

## Merging duplicates

`merge(keepId, dupId)` closes the duplicate (`Ticket.mergedInto()` = kept id) and gives the kept ticket the more urgent priority. Errors in order: same id, unknown id, closed ticket.

DESK-243  Assigning tickets to agents
Type: Feature | Priority: High | Component: queuedesk

Everybody grabs the top ticket from the queue and two agents end up working on the same problem.

  of them as an `Optional<Ticket>`.
* `Desk.close(id)` closes an open ticket and returns it (an already closed ticket is an `IllegalStateException`). `Desk.count(open)`
  counts the open (`true`) or closed (`false`) tickets.

## Reopening tickets

`reopen(id)` opens a closed ticket again (priority and opening tick unchanged); open tickets are an `IllegalStateException`.

## Closing several tickets

`setLimit(agent, max)` (0 removes it) and `limit(agent)`. `assign` refuses an `IllegalStateException` when the agent already owns `max` open tickets (re-assigning to the current owner is fine).

# Design note: Closing several tickets and Ticket tags
Status: approved | Owner: Sunniva

## Closing several tickets
Motivation:
After the outage forty tickets have to be closed one call at a time.

Behaviour:
1. `Desk.closeAll(List<Integer> ids)` closes all the given tickets and returns how many it closed. The list must have 1 to 20 entries without duplicates (`IllegalArgumentException`, checked first). Then the ids are checked in the order given: an unknown id is a `NoSuchElementException`, an already closed ticket an `IllegalStateException`.
2. It is all or nothing: when any check fails no ticket is closed.

## Ticket tags
Motivation:
Support wants to label tickets and list them by label.

Behaviour:
1. `Desk.tag(id, tag)` adds a tag to a ticket (open or closed) and returns whether it was new. A tag is 1 to 12 characters from `a-z`, `0-9` and `-`, not starting with a dash (`IllegalArgumentException`); an unknown ticket is checked first (`NoSuchElementException`). `Desk.untag(id, tag)` removes a tag and returns whether it was there (an unknown ticket is a `NoSuchElementException`, any string is accepted as a tag to remove).
2. `Ticket.tags()` returns a new list of the tags in alphabetical order. `Desk.withTag(tag)` returns the tickets (open or closed) that have the tag, ordered by id.
3. Tagging logs `tagged TAG` and untagging `untagged TAG`, only when the tag set really changed.
4. A merge adds the tags of the duplicate to the kept ticket.

## Out of scope
Anything not described above; everything that works today keeps working as it does. No new dependencies, please.

# Design note: Escalating tickets and Workload limits
Status: approved | Owner: Hana

## Escalating tickets
Motivation:
Support leads need to raise the urgency of a ticket that turned out to be serious.

Behaviour:
1. `Desk.escalate(id)` makes an open ticket one step more urgent (priority minus one) and returns it. A closed ticket and a ticket that already has priority 1 are an `IllegalStateException`; an unknown id is a `NoSuchElementException`. The ticket moves to its new place in the queue.
2. Escalating logs `escalated to pN` with the new priority.
3. Escalating changes the deadline: it is always computed from the opening tick and the current priority.

## Workload limits
Motivation:
One agent has 30 open tickets while the others have two, and nothing stops the lead from piling on more.

Behaviour:
1. `Desk.setLimit(agent, max)` sets how many open tickets an agent may own (`max` 0 removes the limit; a negative `max` or a blank agent is an `IllegalArgumentException`; the agent name is stripped) and `Desk.limit(agent)` returns it (0 means no limit).
2. `assign` fails with an `IllegalStateException` when the agent already owns `max` open tickets, unless the ticket is already owned by that agent (assigning a ticket to its current owner is always fine). This check comes after the checks `assign` already has, and a refused call changes nothing. Closing a ticket frees a slot.
3. `reopen` of a ticket whose agent already owns `max` open tickets is an `IllegalStateException` (the ticket stays closed).

## Out of scope
Anything not described above; everything that works today keeps working as it does.

# Design note: Reopening tickets and Ticket tags
Status: approved | Owner: Dev

## Reopening tickets
Motivation:
Customers reply to closed tickets and support has to open a duplicate by hand.

Behaviour:
1. `Desk.reopen(id)` makes a closed ticket open again and returns it. Priority and opening tick stay as they were. An open ticket is an `IllegalStateException`; an unknown id is a `NoSuchElementException`.
2. `reopen` of a ticket whose agent already owns `max` open tickets is an `IllegalStateException` (the ticket stays closed).
3. Reopening logs `reopened`.
4. A ticket that was merged away cannot be reopened (`IllegalStateException`).

## Ticket tags
Motivation:
Tickets about the VPN are spread over the whole queue and nobody can find them together.

Behaviour:
1. `Desk.tag(id, tag)` adds a tag to a ticket (open or closed) and returns whether it was new. A tag is 1 to 16 characters from `a-z`, `0-9` and `-`, not starting with a dash (`IllegalArgumentException`); an unknown ticket is checked first (`NoSuchElementException`). `Desk.untag(id, tag)` removes a tag and returns whether it was there (an unknown ticket is a `NoSuchElementException`, any string is accepted as a tag to remove).
2. `Ticket.tags()` returns a new list of the tags in alphabetical order. `Desk.withTag(tag)` returns the tickets (open or closed) that have the tag, ordered by id.
3. Tagging logs `tagged TAG` and untagging `untagged TAG`, only when the tag set really changed.
4. A merge adds the tags of the duplicate to the kept ticket.

## Out of scope
Anything not described above; everything that works today keeps working as it does. Please update the README as well.

# Design note: Response deadlines and Merging duplicates
Status: approved | Owner: Sunniva

## Response deadlines
Motivation:
Nobody notices that the urgent tickets have been sitting unanswered for a day.

Behaviour:
1. Every priority has a deadline in ticks after the opening tick: priority 1 gets 1, priority 2 gets 3, priority 3 gets 6 and priority 4 gets 12. `Desk.slaTicks(priority)` is a public static method returning that number (`IllegalArgumentException` outside 1 to 4) and `Desk.deadline(id)` returns `openedAt + slaTicks(priority)` using the ticket's current priority (`NoSuchElementException` for an unknown id).
2. `Desk.breached()` returns the open tickets whose deadline is strictly before `now()`, ordered by deadline and then by id. Closed tickets never appear.

## Merging duplicates
Motivation:
Five customers report the same outage and five agents answer them separately.

Behaviour:
1. `Desk.merge(keepId, dupId)` folds a duplicate ticket into another one and returns the kept ticket. The duplicate gets closed and `Ticket.mergedInto()` returns the id of the kept ticket (an `Integer`, `null` for tickets that were not merged away). The kept ticket takes over the more urgent of the two priorities.
2. Errors in this order: the same id twice (`IllegalArgumentException`), an unknown id (`NoSuchElementException`, `keepId` first), a ticket that is already closed (`IllegalStateException`). A failed merge changes nothing.
3. If the kept ticket has no agent and the duplicate has one, the kept ticket takes over the duplicate's agent (limits, if any, are not checked).

## Out of scope
Anything not described above; everything that works today keeps working as it does.
